Leader results are tested with one created match, so real scoring is only partly covered.

terms.meaning: The part of the app that decides how to answer a question.
Looking up related indexed documents to answer an open question.
A fixed database lookup for a known kind of question.

used_by: Run by the test runner as part of the unit tests.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the database, the planner and crew functions and the test helpers.
sections.why: Provides the tools the planner tests need.

sections.name: query planner: routing
sections.title: Question routing
sections.what: Checks that questions about crew members, crew leaders and a user's crews become structured lookups, that other questions go to retrieval, and that blank or over-long questions are unsupported.
sections.why: Routing decides whether the app answers from the database or refuses, so it must be right.
sections.watch_out: The 300 character limit is a fixed value, and changing it means updating these checks.

sections.name: query planner: answers from the database, phrased by the verified contract
sections.title: Answers from the database
sections.what: Checks that answers are written as sourced sentences, that the answer names the members, that empty cases give an honest explanation, that outsiders are not shown crews they are not in, that open questions are not answered without indexed sources, and that leader answers use completed scored matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: answers must be traceable and must never invent or reveal information.
sections.watch_out: Leader answers depend on the scoring rows, so a change to how completed matches are stored would affect these results.

summary: Tests the query planner, which decides how a user's question is answered: from the database, from indexed sources, or refused.
purpose: Makes sure known question shapes get exact database answers, open questions are not guessed, and users never see crews they are not in.
why: Likely reason: answers should be accurate and sourced, and users should not learn about groups they are outside of.
how: First checks how questions are sorted into structured, retrieval or unsupported routes. Then sets up two crews and users and checks the sentences returned for each type of question, the honest empty messages, and that leader answers come from completed scored matches.
inputs: Plain text questions from a user and seeded users, a crew, and a completed match.
outputs: Answer objects with sentences, sources, an honest empty message, and the plan that was chosen.
risks: Open questions must not reach a language model without indexed sources. The 300 character limit is hard coded in the test. Leader answers depend on a completed match row that the test creates itself.
debug: Check the route the planner picked for the question. If an answer is empty, check the honest message and the crew membership of the user.
